q: The Wyner-Ziv theorem addresses lossy source coding with decoder side information Y. The rate-distortion function with side information is:
opts: R(D) = I(X;X̂) as in the standard case
R(D) = min_{p(x̂|x,y): E[d(X,X̂)]≤D} I(X;X̂|Y), achievable without encoding Y
exp: Wyner-Ziv: R_{X|Y}(D) = min_{p(x̂|x,y): E[d]≤D} I(X;X̂|Y). Remarkably, despite the encoder not having Y, the rate-distortion function equals the case where the encoder has Y (side-information at encoder gives no benefit for Gaussian sources)—the 'Wyner-Ziv theorem'.
